method: Reviewed every responsibility, procedure, hard gate, output, mutation scope, positive trigger, anti-trigger, and holdout against the Phase 2 capability and source provenance.
Computed pairwise positive-trigger lexical overlap at a 0.22 Jaccard review threshold; no candidate pair crossed the threshold.

Reviewed AI capability routing, model/data architecture, agency control, and safety as four separate contracts; reviewed architecture discovery, interface alternatives, deep module design, reporting, and diagrams as separate contracts.
Reviewed authorization, data/API, secrets, CI hardening, frontend runtime, plan review, and threat audit for trust-boundary, secret-value, migration, mutation, and human-authority separation.

resolved_findings.finding: Phase 2 broad workspace-write identities did not distinguish architecture artifacts from authorized product or workflow source mutation.
resolved_findings.resolution: Only CI hardening and frontend runtime safety use authorized-workspace mutation; eleven architecture/security contracts use run-output, two reviewers use none, and the local security audit writes artifact-output only.

resolved_findings.finding: The initial diagram candidate claimed render or syntax validation despite having no local-exec permission.
resolved_findings.resolution: It now emits diagram source, structural checks, and an exact host render or syntax-validation request; it cannot claim renderer evidence before host execution.

resolved_findings.finding: Secret governance could be mistaken for permission to inspect or hash values for evidence.
resolved_findings.resolution: All candidates prohibit requesting, reading, printing, copying, transforming, hashing, persisting, or transmitting secret values; verification uses names, references, metadata, policy, and behavior only.

resolved_findings.finding: The combined source material risked treating AI capability choice, model/data design, autonomy, and safety as one giant AI architecture workflow.
resolved_findings.resolution: AI capability routing performs no specialist design; model/data, action rights and human control, user interaction, and safety each retain separate inputs, gates, outputs, and decision owners.

boundary_samples.boundary: Capability architecture classifies specialist needs and unresolved coupling only; model/data architecture chooses bounded model, prompt, retrieval, governed-data, evaluation, migration, and rollback contracts.
Agency defines action rights, graduation, interruption, rollback, revocation, and fallback; safety independently challenges prompt, data, tool, and action abuse paths and cannot approve autonomy.

Discovery cites recurring friction and preserves leave-unchanged options; deep module design begins only from a selected candidate and specifies one boundary, interface, invariants, seams, migration, and tests.
Alternative evaluation generates structurally independent interfaces and tradeoffs; reporting only normalizes already-developed candidates against common evidence and criteria.
Diagram generation represents approved facts and marks unknowns; it cannot discover architecture facts, run a renderer, or convert syntax validity into factual validity.

Authorization owns subject-resource-action-context policy and server enforcement; data/API design owns schemas, invariants, migration, request and response behavior, idempotency, concurrency, compatibility, and authorization hooks.

Secrets governance defines value-free lifecycle policy across environments; CI hardening may patch only authorized workflow source to enforce least privilege, isolate untrusted input, pin actions, and protect identities and artifacts.
Frontend runtime safety keeps secrets, server modules, and privileged logic out of clients; authorization defines the server-side policy that remains authoritative even when UI hides actions.
Threat audit may run approved local non-destructive checks and write evidence artifacts; it never edits source, accesses secrets, performs destructive tests, accepts risk, or executes remediation.

Engineering plan review checks proposed architecture, data, security, failure, operability, migration, and test coverage from documents; threat audit assesses supplied actual system evidence and authorized checks.

release_claim: none; all 16 candidates remain evaluating and all evaluation plans remain not-run-phase-9
